clue.text: Cheese and soft, green fruit regularly not out

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction meaning soft
eco- means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: every other letter of the word fruit is taken, the rest left aside
with regularly, says alternate letters of fruit are put out

parts.note: no can mean not, as in 'no better'

explanation.surface: A shopper wants cheese and some soft green fruit, but finds it is not in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ... out' keeps the even letters R and I of 'fruit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian sheep's-milk variety, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Or Adams short work, And Another Thing … Guides for hitchhikers?

indicators.note: work tells us to rework the letters into a new order
short means the last letter of Adams is cut off

parts.note: a postscript, PS, adds another thing to a letter; also the title of the sixth Hitchhiker book

explanation.surface: A nod to Douglas Adams's Hitchhiker's Guide books, including And Another Thing, the sequel by Eoin Colfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And Another Thing' looks like the book title but works as a postscript, added after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists and hitchhikers alike use printed charts of routes to find their way, so they are guides for travellers.

clue.text: US restaurant at end of universe with English lines for cover

indicators.note: E and RY act as a cover wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of universe

explanation.surface: Points to The Restaurant at the End of the Universe, the Hitchhiker sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows a book title; 'for cover' wraps English and lines around 'at' plus the final letter of universe. RY (railway) for lines is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery is an informal, originally American word for a place serving meals.

clue.text: Country and its location left for study

parts.note: Peru is a South American nation
Peru lies in South America, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A geography question: name a country and say where it lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its location' is the continent of the country, South America, SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, the same as a study of something.

clue.text: Lack job, love to go to the top

indicators.note: in a down light the top is the start, so this piece is placed first

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a mission is an assigned task or job

explanation.surface: Someone without work dreams of love and climbing the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, a want or absence of it.

clue.text: Big edition ran spread

indicators.note: spread says the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A newspaper's large print run was distributed widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means excessive or unusually large, so it stands for big.

clue.text: Adventure mostly harmless and dry

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept, applying to both words

parts.note: safe means harmless, posing no danger
arid means dry

explanation.surface: Mostly Harmless is a Hitchhiker book; here a dry, mostly harmless trip.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'mostly' serves both words: each of SAFE and ARID loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition into the wild, typically in Africa, a kind of adventure.

clue.text: One to cut French daily drink

indicators.note: the single letter cuts into the newspaper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a Paris daily newspaper
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone gets a French newspaper and a drink, as in a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft beverage made with lemons.

clue.text: Many? Not so long and thanks for fish

indicators.note: not so long means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Echoes So Long, and Thanks for All the Fish, the fourth Hitchhiker book.
explanation.definitionFit: The manta is a huge ray, a cartilaginous sea creature counted among the fishes.

clue.text: In the 1980s, perhaps, one picking up hitchhiker's guide to galaxy?

definitions.text: In the 1980s, perhaps, one picking up hitchhiker's guide to galaxy?

parts.words: In the 1980s, perhaps, one picking up hitchhiker's guide to galaxy
parts.note: A popular 1980s hatchback by the same maker might pick up a hitchhiker

explanation.surface: A driver of a 1980s car picks up a hitchhiking Ford Prefect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Escort was a common British family car of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The car is a model that gave lifts in the 1980s, and an escort is also a guide.

clue.text: Queen at start of race is changing jockey?

indicators.note: changing says the letters swap into a new order
start of picks the first letter of race

explanation.surface: The Queen arrives at the start of a race meeting as things shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is a horse rider, and an equestrian is someone skilled on horseback; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Pen good section with feel for describing

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line around, so pity encircles the letters

parts.note: to pity is to feel for someone

explanation.surface: A writer's advice: pen a good section showing sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for animals, and a sty is one for pigs.

clue.text: Is nautical tour to show island?

indicators.note: a tour goes round, sending the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a sailing trip would display a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Caribbean nation in the Windward chain of islands.

clue.text: Selected by The X Factor, a person's story's entertaining from the beginning

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a bio is a biography, a person's life story
a player picked for a team is in
it is that indefinable special quality, the X factor

explanation.surface: A TV talent show contestant's backstory wins over the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 's of "story's" is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ab initio is Latin meaning starting right at the outset.

clue.text: Prefect reversing in car outside

indicators.note: the vehicle goes outside, enclosing the letters

parts.note: motor is a British word for a car

indicators.note: reversing means the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Ford Prefect, of Hitchhiker fame, is reversing in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prefect' looks like the Ford car; it is a school prefect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil appointed to keep order in a school is a prefect, also called a monitor.

clue.text: Toes cracking? It's a problem with bone

indicators.note: cracking breaks the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: it's expands to it is

explanation.surface: Someone's toes are cracking and fears a skeletal complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: This is inflammation of bony tissue, a medical complaint of the skeleton.

clue.text: Find short Arthur Dent's stripped off

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged
short means the last letter of Arthur is dropped
stripped removes the outer letters, leaving the middle of Dent

explanation.surface: Arthur Dent, hero of the Hitchhiker books, has his clothes taken.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTHU and EN are shuffled together; 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it.

clue.text: Great time having sex

parts.note: humping is slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about a good time in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumping is an informal intensifier for very large, as in a thumping majority.

clue.text: Camels go out here? Hot, missing covers

indicators.note: the word for missing covers, enclosing, the letter

parts.note: astray means lost or missing

explanation.surface: Desert camels wander off in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Camel is a cigarette brand, so camels are stubbed out in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarettes are extinguished in a dish for ash, so Camels go out there.

clue.text: Apes left pair of primates to go around island by Thailand

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the other letters
the first two letters on the left side of the word primates
to go says those letters are removed

parts.note: T is Thailand's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A zoo scene: two primates leave, wandering round an island near Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIMATES loses PR to give IMATES; I and T go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so apes is a verb meaning copies.

clue.text: Sweet American dear by the sounds of it?

indicators.note: the plural sounds marks two sound-alikes, dear for deer and the animal for the dessert

parts.note: dear sounds like deer, and the elk of North America is called a moose

explanation.surface: A sweet American darling, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert is a sweet course.

clue.text: Drink, leaving head to settle

indicators.note: the first letter departs from the word

parts.note: 7 Up is a brand of lemon-lime soft drink

explanation.surface: A drinker leaves the froth to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up a score or account is to square it, i.e. to settle.

clue.text: See 10
Endlessly amusing for visitors, not old, like 25?

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: fun means amusing

indicators.note: not says the following letter is removed

parts.note: touristic means aimed at tourists

explanation.surface: Something entertaining for tourists, modern, like science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is often set in times to come, so it is forward-looking in style.

clue.text: See 2
Show behind heartless idiot

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter

parts.note: a moron is a stupid person

explanation.surface: An idiot with no heart bares his bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare one's buttocks as an insult is the slang verb meaning flash the bottom.

clue.text: Some terrific stuff in retrospect: like Life, the Universe and Everything?

definitions.text: like Life, the Universe and Everything?

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so read backwards
some means part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Praise for Life, the Universe and Everything, the third Hitchhiker book.
explanation.definitionFit: That novel is science fiction, the genre the question asks about.

clue.text: Flying first class, queen goes to island, briefly

parts.note: A1 is first class, written AI
R is Regina, queen

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter

parts.note: Borneo is a large Asian island

explanation.surface: A queen travels to an island in first class for a short stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read with I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne describes something in the air, i.e. aloft.
